item.name: Trip Search (Gateway)
item.description:
TA-17 one-way search: `GET /api/v1/trips/search`.

Requires a verified traveller, so run **Authentication (Gateway) > Sign In**
first -- these requests inherit the bearer `{{accessToken}}` it stores. There is
no guest mode.

The station, travel-class and train-number variables are the fixed ids of the
catalog search fixture; load it with `npm run catalog:seed:search` after catalog
has migrated. `{{searchDepartureDate}}` is filled in automatically with the Cairo
date three days out (the day the fixture puts trips on) whenever it is left blank.

Every response uses the platform envelope: `success`, `data`, `error`. A refusal
names the field to change in `error.details[].field`; a 503 or 504 from a slow or
stopped catalog carries `error.retryAfterSeconds`.

request.description:
One-way search for a day, a station pair and one travel class.

Answers trips ordered for the traveller, a five-day date strip around the
searched date, the booking window behind it, and the Cairo moment it was
evaluated at. Fares are integer piastres excluding the booking fee, and
durations come from instants, so an overnight or DST-crossing trip is still
correct.

Cached per identical request, so two travellers asking the same thing get the
same answer; with Redis down it is served the slow way, never refused.

request.description: The global validation pipe forbids parameters the DTO does not declare, so a typo or a stale client fails loudly instead of being silently ignored.

Search has no guest mode, which is also what makes the results cacheable:
they are identical for every caller.

The token is verified at the edge against a public key, so identity being
down does not stop a traveller searching -- and a malformed token is a 401
here, not a 500.
